A1.justification: Both complete, readable 29-page PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on 17 multi-agent tasks in Section 4 and original Craftax results in Appendix C.1, Table 1.

after.justification: v3 reports original multi-agent experiments, including revised inference-strategy comparisons, and retains the original Craftax experiment in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: Section 3.2, Appendix F.2, and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same sampling, SGBS, fine-tuning, and COMPASS procedures. The revised results are not accompanied by a documented algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 RWARE tasks, two Connector tasks, two SMACv2 tasks, and Craftax-1B in Appendix C.1. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain IPPO, MAPPO, and SABLE with greedy inference and the same four inference strategies. Newly cited SPO is discussed as related work but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The stated protocols retain the 30-second comparison with 64 parallel attempts, the budget sweep up to 300 seconds and 256 parallel attempts, and the same metrics and training budgets. No protocol revision explaining the changed plots is documented.

E4.justification: The existing budget-sensitivity analyses in Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix A receive revised evidence, particularly replacing SGBS's broadly time-insensitive contours with stronger time-dependent performance. The tested questions remain the same; no new ablation, robustness test, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: The 128-seed evaluations, IQM aggregation, and 95% bootstrap confidence-interval practices are retained, as is Appendix L's run-count information. Changed interval values in the revised plots do not establish a change in statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 5–8 substantially revise SGBS results and also change some other methods' plotted scores. Under Figure 7's stated 300-second setting, SGBS's normalized IQM at 256 parallel attempts changes from approximately 0.55 to 0.79. Figure 8 changes SGBS from weak performance to the leading method on smacv2_10_units. Craftax results and Table 17 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Dec-POMDP definition, training objective, and constrained inference objective remain mathematically equivalent. Section 3.1 shortens explanatory wording without changing assumptions, definitions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the unified inference-strategy contribution, the reported average 45% and maximum 126% improvements, and the main claims about inference-time search and COMPASS scaling.

C2.justification: The practical assessment of SGBS is substantially recast. v2 attributes its inability to exploit additional time to greedy simulations and groups it with frequently underperforming fine-tuning. v3 removes that explanation, emphasizes competitive performance and leadership in some low-budget regimes, and identifies Connector failures instead. This reverses important strategy-selection guidance; the broader applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, implementation libraries, hyperparameter tables, training budgets, parameter counts, pseudocode, and code/data access statements are retained. No new implementation or reproducibility information explains the revised SGBS results.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Macfarlane et al. (2024), SPO: Sequential Monte Carlo Policy Optimisation, with a sentence connecting it to inference-time policy improvement through sequential updates. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Noah De Nicola to the author list, changes another author's name spelling, and makes localized prose edits in related work, preliminaries, and experimental discussion. Section ordering and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 5–8 are regenerated with revised graphical content and small changes to plot sizing and label placement. Text and references undergo limited page reflow; figure and table inventories and panel organization remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful qualifications about SGBS and relevant prior work. However, substantial score revisions lack an accompanying methodological explanation, and Section 4.2's retained broad COMPASS-dominance statement is not fully reconciled with the newly acknowledged SGBS-leading regimes. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the revised comparisons and discussion yield a reliable net quality improvement.
